set.body:
Objective:
Evolve Sojourn from its compositional batch/store foundation into a resource-aware remote-execution layer with sound Slurm lowering, resource-aware pilot pools, backend-neutral provenance and telemetry, and explicitly safe persistent memoization.

Architectural rule:
Sojourn owns portable computation, data, task, pool, lease, outcome, and publication semantics. sojourn-slurm compiles those semantics into provider requests and projects provider evidence. scala-slurm owns Slurm resource and placement resolution, durable attempts, scheduler interaction, worker evidence, result attachment, accounting, and cancellation. remote-exec-kernel remains limited to genuinely provider-neutral identities, codecs, diagnostics, retry declarations, digests, and atomic publication.

Child epics:
- soj-exec-epic: portable execution requirements, durable Slurm planning, and resource-aware pools.
- soj-ops-epic: task-record projection, bounded telemetry, opt-in memoization, and lightweight composition.

Borrow/adapt/defer decisions from vendor/tasks:
- Adapt requested/available/allocated resource separation with stronger types.
- Adopt bounded OpenTelemetry after a typed TaskRecord projection exists.
- Adopt persistent memoization only as an explicit operation contract.
- Retain RemoteRef and ArtifactSet rather than introducing a second file abstraction.
- Use resource matching inside pilot pools rather than creating a competing Slurm queue.
- Defer PostgreSQL queueing, elastic SSH/EC2/Kubernetes worker management, and a DAG database until a concrete non-Slurm requirement exists.
- Do not adopt closure serialization, default caching, loose labels, string option bags, or a duplicate execution receipt.

Existing authorities:
- SCOMP.6 remains authoritative for durable declared artifacts.
- S3 remains authoritative for disposable or configured Slurm-controller StoreTck and BatchTck acceptance evidence; this roadmap must reference rather than duplicate it.

Completion criteria:
- Both child epics are closed with their focused acceptance evidence.
- sojourn-core retains no scala-slurm dependency or provider-specific types.
- Requested portable requirements and effective provider allocation are both inspectable and durably replayable.
- Local, Slurm batch, and Slurm pool backends satisfy the applicable published TCK laws.
- Provenance and metrics are projections from authoritative state, not competing journals.
- Memoization never serves unverified, indeterminate, interrupted, failed, or partially published outcomes.
- Cross-repository source pins, focused tests, repository-wide compile/test/format gates, codec golden tests, and proportional live-controller evidence are recorded.
set.title: EPIC: Build resource-aware, observable, memoized Sojourn execution
